history: Mount Panorama, Bathurst, is a legendary Australian motor racing circuit steeped in history. Opened in 1938, it was initially conceived as a scenic tourist drive, but it quickly evolved into a challenging and iconic race track. The Full Circuit configuration, the primary and most well-known layout, has hosted countless races, most famously the Bathurst 1000, a grueling endurance race for touring cars that has become a cornerstone of Australian motorsport. Beyond the Bathurst 1000, the track hosts a variety of other events, including the Bathurst 12 Hour, a GT endurance race, and various club-level and national series races.
atmosphere: Standing at the top of Mount Panorama during the Bathurst 1000 is an experience unlike any other. The roar of the engines echoes through the valleys, reverberating off the surrounding hills. The air is thick with anticipation and the smell of racing fuel. Crowds throng the campgrounds, their cheers rising and falling with the fortunes of their favorite drivers. The sight of the cars cresting Skyline and diving down into the Esses is simply breathtaking, a visual spectacle that perfectly encapsulates the thrill and danger of motorsport.
trackCharacter: The Mount Panorama Full Circuit is a demanding and unforgiving track, a true test of driver skill and car setup. Its unique combination of high-speed straights, challenging corners, and significant elevation changes makes it unlike any other circuit in the world. The first sector is defined by the climb up the mountain, a narrow, winding section with little room for error. The descent is equally treacherous, demanding precision and bravery. The final sector is a more flowing section, but still requires commitment and accuracy. The Full Circuit is a relentless challenge that rewards bravery, precision, and a well-balanced car.

famousCorners.name: Hell Corner
famousCorners.description: The first corner after the start/finish line, a tight right-hander that has witnessed countless accidents over the years.
famousCorners.challenge: Navigating the first-lap melee and avoiding contact while positioning for the climb up the mountain.

famousCorners.name: The Cutting
famousCorners.description: A narrow, uphill left-hander that requires precise placement and commitment.
famousCorners.challenge: Maintaining momentum and avoiding the inside wall, which can easily ruin a lap or end a race.

famousCorners.name: Forrest's Elbow
famousCorners.description: A very slow, almost hairpin-like right-hander that interrupts the high-speed descent.
famousCorners.challenge: Braking late and accurately, while avoiding locking the wheels and running wide.

famousCorners.name: The Dipper
famousCorners.description: A fast, downhill left-hander that requires nerves of steel.
famousCorners.challenge: Maintaining speed and control through the compression, while avoiding running wide onto the exit kerb.

famousCorners.name: Conrod Straight
famousCorners.description: One of the longest straights in Australian motorsport, offering high speeds and overtaking opportunities.
famousCorners.challenge: Managing engine temperatures and fuel consumption, while preparing for the braking zone at The Chase.

keyFactors: Engine Power (for the climb and straights)
overtakingSpots: The Chase (at the end of Conrod Straight)
historySnippets: The first race at Mount Panorama was held in 1938.
The Bathurst 1000 is traditionally held in October.
The lap record for the Full Circuit is held by Chaz Mostert.
Mount Panorama is one of the most challenging circuits in the world.
The circuit is named after the mountain it is built on.
The circuit is a public road when not in use for racing.
weatherNotes: Bathurst weather can be unpredictable, with conditions often changing rapidly. Rain is common, especially during the autumn and winter months, which can make the track extremely slippery. Fog can also be a factor, especially in the early morning, reducing visibility and adding to the challenge. The heat during summer races puts huge stress on the drivers and the machinery.
drivingAdvice: At Bathurst, respect the Mountain. Don't overdrive the car, especially on the first few laps. Build up your speed gradually and learn the track's nuances. Be patient in traffic and choose your overtaking opportunities wisely. Conserve your tires and brakes, as they will be put to the test. Most importantly, stay out of trouble and bring the car home in one piece.
famousRaces: 1979 Bathurst 1000: Peter Brock and Jim Richards win in a dominant display, setting a new lap record in the process.
2003 Bathurst 1000: Greg Murphy sets the 'Lap of the Gods', a stunning qualifying lap that remains one of the most iconic moments in Bathurst history.
2014 Bathurst 1000: Chaz Mostert wins in dramatic fashion, passing Jamie Whincup on the final lap after a late-race safety car period.
localCulture: Bathurst is a vibrant regional city with a rich history and a strong connection to motorsport. The city comes alive during race events, with fans flocking from all over Australia and the world. The local pubs and restaurants are packed with fans, sharing stories and celebrating the sport. Paddock life is a friendly and welcoming atmosphere, with teams and drivers interacting with fans and signing autographs. The local food scene is diverse, with plenty of options to suit all tastes, from traditional pub fare to fine dining.
